:activity/steps [{:db/id 17592186079589 :step/content {:db/id 17592186079714 :tutorial/content "Let's take a look at the following algebraic expression:
$2x{\,\color{red}{-}\,} 4y {\,\color{blue}{+}\,} 7$
The addition $({\color{blue}{+}})$ and subtraction $({\color{red}{-}})$ symbols separate this expression into three parts known as **terms**.

To identify each term, we put an addition symbol $({\color{blue}{+}})$ between each part and separate using parentheses:

$$
(2x) {\,\color{blue}{+}\,} ({\,\color{red}{-}\,} 4y) {\,\color{blue}{+}\,} (7)
$$

So, the terms of this expression are:
$2x,\quad -4y,\quad \quad 7$
We say that $2x$ is the **first term**, $-4y$ is the **second term**, and $7$ is the **third term**.

In this example, the subtraction symbol gave us the term $-4y$. Whenever there is a subtraction symbol, the corresponding term will be negative." :tutorial/id #uuid "a3fedc83-1abf-5dae-af95-68dd8069bf3e" :tutorial/math-academy-id 8035 :tutorial/title "Introduction"} :step/id #uuid "f8931686-8ab0-55f7-ac91-27963af09ae5" :step/math-academy-id 75175 :step/next {:db/id 17592186079590}} {:db/id 17592186079590 :step/content {:db/id 17592186078613 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186078158 :question/id #uuid "65cb74a2-b55a-58e7-951d-2e0c09662f68" :question/math-academy-id "e-12823"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "ffb52c1b-a540-5255-8c13-a37940a0d6ec" :knowledge-point/key-prerequisites [{:db/id 17592186050618} {:db/id 17592186051009}] :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186078812} {:db/id 17592186079038} {:db/id 17592186079039}] :knowledge-point/title "Listing the Terms of a Linear Expression"} :step/id #uuid "d3ccacbe-b3b1-59d6-aca9-544e52d96477" :step/math-academy-id 75176 :step/next {:db/id 17592186079591}} {:db/id 17592186079591 :step/content {:db/id 17592186078614 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186078159 :question/id #uuid "4370fda3-97e7-5fc5-9459-4176f5922431" :question/math-academy-id "e-12824"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "da99f266-f47f-5fda-8b91-2161c7e48a94" :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186078900} {:db/id 17592186078901} {:db/id 17592186079175}] :knowledge-point/title "Identifying Particular Terms of an Expression"} :step/id #uuid "a41ca648-ff16-5981-9555-fc4f21dbf835" :step/math-academy-id 75180 :step/next {:db/id 17592186079592}} {:db/id 17592186079592 :step/content {:db/id 17592186079715 :tutorial/content "When two algebraic expressions contain exactly the same terms, they are said to be **equivalent**.

${\color{blue}{x}} + {\color{red}{2y}} + 3z$
is equivalent to
$3z+{\color{blue}{x}} + {\color{red}{2y}}$
because they both contain the exact same terms. Both expressions are also equivalent to
